rows.source: HSE Electricity at Work Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Electrical systems must be constructed and maintained so far as reasonably practicable to prevent danger.
Electrical equipment must be maintained in a condition that prevents danger.
Employers must control risks arising from the use of electricity at work.
Work on or near electrical equipment requires safe working practices appropriate to the task and system.
Electrical work should use safe isolation and avoid live working where reasonably practicable.
Isolation arrangements should prevent inadvertent re-energisation while work is carried out.
Safe isolation includes proving that conductors are dead using suitable procedures and equipment.

rows.source: HSE Electricity at Work Regulations guidance
rows.verified: People working on electrical systems must have the knowledge or experience needed to prevent danger or be appropriately supervised.
Users should make simple visual checks and report damage or defects before equipment is used.
Damaged or defective electrical equipment should be taken out of use until made safe.
Inspection and maintenance arrangements should reflect equipment type, use and operating environment.
Portable appliance testing frequency is not a universal annual legal requirement and should be risk based.
Residual current devices can provide supplementary protection but do not replace safe installation and working practices.
Wet, confined or harsh environments can increase electrical risk and require suitable equipment and controls.
Electrical test equipment and probes must be suitable for the system and designed to reduce shock and short-circuit risks.
Hazardous installations should be designed to fail to a safe state on loss of power unless maintaining power is necessary for safety.
Electrical protection devices require appropriate maintenance so their safety function remains available.
Inspection and test intervals depend on equipment, environment, use and previous results rather than a single universal timetable.
Safe-isolation arrangements must match the actual circuit, energy sources and work activity.
Workplace electrical controls describe dutyholder practice and are not converted into parcel-level safety probability.
